title: Running Pee Wee and Art's Back Room, 1949
summary: Pee Wee knows a bar owner who gives them the Back Room. They book Jack Teagarden and add Chippy Hill and bassist Herb Ward at $75. Hodes was paid $30 a week.

blocks.x: And on the way, Pee Wee says, I know a man. I says, let's stop in, so we stopped in to see him. And he had a bar, it was the Back Room. And there was nothing happening in the Back Room. So Pee Wee says, how about letting us have the Back Room? And the boss says, fine, it's yours, go ahead and do whatever you want with it.

So he put up a sign above his awning, Pee Wee and Art's Back Room. And within the end of the week, he gave us $30 a week apiece, advance. Meanwhile, we were hiring a bass player, Herb Ward, at $75 a week. So we'd have a trio. At least, two would play and then Pee Wee would come in and so forth. So anyway, we lasted over a year, and then that whole year we booked Jack Teagarden with his band -- Louis Armstrong was having his teeth taken out or fixed and the band was laid off. Jack did a week, did eight days there. And that was a real --
I never knew that, I . . . never read anything about it.
